newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian aluminium plants may cut output.
newsitem.headline: Russian aluminium plants may cut output.

text.p: Russia's top aluminium producers may agree to curb production, but levels have not yet been set, Oleg Deripaska, chief executive officer of Sayansk Aluminium, told Reuters on Friday.

"I expect a decision to be taken to not hold output at present levels but to decrease production at Bratsk, Sayansk and Krasnoyarsk after the Kontsern Aluminy producers' group meets," Deripaska said by telephone. He had no details on when the meeting would take place.
A Canadian diplomat in Moscow said that Russian and Canadian government officials had recently meet to discuss curbing Russian output.
"There is no final word on the negotiations," said the diplomat, who declined to be named.

"We expect there will be some settlement of the issue. It is a question of final approvals -- we think it will be soon," he said, adding that negotiations with Russian officials had gone "fairly well".
A two-year global output cutting deal was signed in March 1994 by major producers Russia, Australia, Canada, the European Union, Norway and the United States.
The memorandum of understanding (MOU), signed to cut output by 10 percent, ended earlier this year.
Producers other than Russia had said the MOU was needed because of weak fundamentals and because Russia had been flooding the market with cheap supplies.
Russian output of primary aluminium over January-August was 1.88 million tonnes, a 2.3 percent rise on 1995 levels, according to Kontsern Aluminiy.
Russia's January-August aluminium exports outside the Commonwealth of Independent States were over 1.75 million tonnes, according to State Customs Committee figures.
Russian smelters had said in January that they might boost output when the MOU expired.
